title: Compliance Analyst - Senior Compliance Analyst
description:
Important Application Submission Information
In order to ensure your application is successfully received before the job posting expires, please submit your application by 11:59 PM on Saturday, September 26, 2026
More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

Position Summary

Compliance Analyst
This is the second level of the Compliance Analyst classification hierarchy. Employees at this level solve problems, in single areas of specialization, with general supervision. Incumbents are expected to develop skills, and the ability to work with greater independence, as well as strive to become subject matter experts. They have knowledge of fundamental concepts and understand how to develop and apply procedures while balancing Duke Energy’s internal (e.g., IT502, IT503) and external regulatory compliance requirements (e.g., FERC, NERC, NIST, Sarbanes Oxley) and the needs of the business.

Sr Compliance Analyst
This is the third level of the Compliance Analyst classification hierarchy.  Employees at this level solve more complex problems, in multiple areas of specialization, with general supervision.  Incumbents are expected to develop advanced skills and the ability to work with greater independence. They effectively apply fundamental concepts and procedures to work that is fairly complex and varied. They have knowledge of fundamental concepts and understand how to develop and apply procedures while balancing Duke Energy’s internal (e.g., IT502, IT503) and external regulatory compliance requirements (e.g., FERC, NERC, NIST, Sarbanes Oxley) and the needs of the business

Responsibilities

Compliance Program Support

- Carries out individual work assignments in development and support of processes, programs, and projects of the Compliance program.

- Gather and review data for responses to legal and regulatory inquiries.

- Demonstrates working knowledge of external and internal regulatory standards, policies, processes, and controls that are appliable to the business area.

- Perform or assist in business area trending analysis and reporting.

- Guide and support business units in the development of self-reports, cause analyses, corrective plans, and mitigation plan porting.

- Competent in the use of compliance tracking tools, procedures, and research capabilities for the Compliance program.

- Correlate incident data to identify specific vulnerabilities and make recommendations that enable expeditious remediation.

- Assess or assist in the assessment in the effectiveness of internal compliance controls.

- Maintain or create evidence of mitigation and corrective actions and required business area reporting .

- Correlate event data to identify trends and compliance risks.  Make recommendations that enable expeditious remediation to events and prevents recurrence. Project Management

- Carries out individual work assignments of a more complex nature for project related to implementing changes to support new or revised standards.

- Receives work assignments and works independently with some review and direction by management or senior compliance analyst.

- Performs or assists in the performance of technical project work as needed to complete project deliverables.

- Works directly with internal project leads to ensure project goals are met and/or issues are escalated, classified, and documented properly. Process and Controls Awareness

- Working knowledge of Compliance policies, standards, processes, and controls.

- Able to apply process and controls knowledge to meet compliance requirements.

- Provides input on process improvements to Compliance program.

- Executes Compliance functional processes and procedures with minimal oversight.

- Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of program controls to ensure they provide the intended level of protections. Customer Relationship Management

- Communicate with customers to understand compliance / regulatory requirements.

- Communicate compliance information in a clear and concise manner.

- Communicate problems and resolutions to manager and/or customers.

- Provides good customer support to deliver compliance results to internal parties.

Required/Basic Qualifications - Compliance Analyst

- Bachelors degree in Computer Science or

- Bachelors degree in Economics or

- Bachelors degree in Engineering or

- Bachelors degree in Business or

- Bachelors degree in Accounting or

- Bachelors degree in Cybersecurity or

- Bachelors degree in Other Related Degree or

- Bachelors degree in Computer Information Systems or

- Bachelors degree in Finance

- 2 years related work experience

- In lieu of Bachelors degree(s) AND 2 year(s) related work experience listed above, High School/GED AND 6 year(s) related work experience

Required/Basic Qualifications - Sr Compliance Analyst

- Bachelors degree in Computer Science or

- Bachelors degree in Economics or

- Bachelors degree in Engineering or

- Bachelors degree in Business or

- Bachelors degree in Accounting or

- Bachelors degree in Cybersecurity or

- Bachelors degree in Other Related Degree or

- Bachelors degree in Computer Information Systems or

- Bachelors degree in Finance

- 4 years related work experience

- In lieu of Bachelors degree(s) AND 4 year(s) related work experience listed above, High School/GED AND 8 year(s) related work experience

​
Desired Qualifications

- Bachelors degree

Additional Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with audit skills, controls, security, and related industry regulatory issues

- Demonstrates excellent listening and communication skills and puts forth the effort to understand other points of view

- Has the ability to manage confidential information with a high degree of integrity

- Responds well to supervisors, is easy to challenge and develop, and is easily coachable

- Able to work effectively with minimally defined direction requiring some degree of judgment

- Able to present complex information in an understandable manner both verbal and written

- Demonstrated ability to absorb change and continue with positive results

- Exhibits confidence and a proper level of assertiveness when needed; displays maturity in approach and ability to effectively handle stress and frustration

- Recognize a possible compliance violation and take appropriate action to report the incident as required

- Knowledge in validating the organization against policies/guidelines/procedures/regulations/laws to ensure compliance

- Skill in supporting audits or reviews of technical systems.

- Skill in performing impact/risk assessments.

- Skill in processing collected data for follow-on analysis.

- Previous experience in regulatory compliance, risk management, audit, accounting/finance, or other relevant positions

- Understanding of utility industry operations

- PE, PMP, CISA (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency), CISSP (Certified Information System Security Professional), NERC System Operator, CPA, CIA (Certified Internal Auditor), CPSM (Certified Professional Supply Management)

Working Conditions

- Onsite Mobility Classification – Work will be performed at a company facility. On-site employees are also required to live within a reasonable daily commute to their assigned work location, not greater than 50 miles one way.

Specific Requirements

- If NERC CIP access is required, a Personal Risk Assessment will need to be completed every 7 years and annual cybersecurity training must be successfully completed as well.

Travel Requirements
5-15%
Relocation Assistance Provided (as applicable)
Yes
Represented/Union Position
No
Visa Sponsored Position
No. This is not a Visa Sponsored Position. This role requires the ability to work lawfully in the U.S. without employment-based immigration sponsorship, now or in the future.

Please note that in order to be considered for this position, you must possess all of the basic/required qualifications.

Important Application Submission Information
In order to ensure your application is successfully received before the job posting expires, please submit your application by 11:59 PM on Tuesday, September 22, 2026
More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

Job Summary

The Rates and Regulatory Strategy Manager will play an integral role in supporting regulatory activities and initiatives for Duke Energy’s regulated electric utilities in North Carolina and South Carolina. This position requires a strong understanding of regulated utility accounting and finance, coupled with a strategic approach to advancing business objectives within a complex regulatory environment.

The successful applicant should be able to support and manage major work streams and work independently to keep processes on track to successful completion.  They should be able to provide guidance to others (both internal and external to the group) and collaborate effectively with others within the Company.  They will have a grasp on industry issues and emerging rules and proactively address how these issues may affect regulatory processes and adhere to proper ratemaking treatment.  Developing good working relationships with internal and external customer groups is important.  Must be proficient in conflict management and know how to listen attentively, as well as be able to communicate both orally and in written form proficiently. Must be able to present ideas and concepts clearly to broad groups.

Key Responsibilities

- Support Performance Based Ratemaking (“PBR”) recovery mechanisms such as Multi-Year Rate Plan (“MYRP”), Earnings Sharing Mechanism (“ESM”), decoupling, and performance incentive mechanisms.  This includes supporting monthly processes to monitor MYRP execution, preparing and reviewing required quarterly and annual reports filed with the Commission as well as internal reports used to support various internal governance activities and meetings.

- Participate and help lead cross functional teams supporting the MYRP governance and reporting activities.  Serve as a point of contact for operational teams for regulatory guidance related to MYRP and PBR recovery mechanisms.

- Prepare annual PBR reports and rider updates.  This includes working with operations to obtain supporting workpapers, calculating revenue requirements and determining rate changes, preparing the filing, and supporting the discovery process related to the filings.

- Support general rate cases by engaging in activities such as strategizing, researching, performing calculations and analysis, providing data requests,  reviewing and drafting testimony and exhibits.

- Effectively communicate regulatory and cost recovery concepts to both internal and external audiences, including internal management, external regulators, and customers.

- Support other riders, proforma calculations, or analysis, as needed, within the Carolinas Rates and Regulatory team.

Basic / Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business, mathematics or other related degree

- In addition to bachelor's degree, eight (8) years minimum of related work experience

Desired Qualifications

- Experience in utility and/or regulatory work.

- Familiarity with ratemaking concepts and principles (e.g. revenue requirement).

- Project management skills.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint; including ability to develop and use complex spreadsheets using advanced techniques

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Proven analytical and problem-solving abilities.

- Keen attention to detail, with the ability to identify data irregularities and maintain a high level of accuracy.

- Ability to influence others and gain support for proposals and recommendations.

- Strong time management skills, with the capacity to meet deadlines and work independently with minimal supervision.

- Ability to foster effective working relationships.

- Background in finance, regulatory accounting, data analysis, or project management

- Advanced degree and/or professional certification (i.e., MBA, CPA).

Working Conditions

- Hybrid Mobility Classification – Work will be performed from both remote and onsite locations after the onboarding period. However, hybrid employees must live within a reasonable commute to their designated Duke Energy facility, not greater than 50 miles one way. Employees are expected to report to their assigned Duke Energy facility as required and directed by their manager, on average 3 full workdays per regular workweek.

- Primarily a normal office environment with extensive use of a computer.

- Ability to work remotely two days per week.

- Minimal travel required.

- Overtime may be necessary to meet deadlines, particularly during regulatory proceedings (e.g. rate case).

description:
Important Application Submission Information

More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

The Transmission Contracts Analyst (or Senior) is responsible for execution of the Transmission Provider (TP) activities and support of Duke Energy initiatives regarding the TP function. Key responsibilities include supporting Duke Energy's Transmission Owner (TO) functions, providing input into business practices supporting the TP and TO functions, monitoring TP and TO filings and business practices, monitoring the regulatory environment for changes in rules, and representing Duke Energy concerning TP and TO issues. The Transmission Contracts Analyst (or Senior) also has a variety of operational responsibilities, including providing support during emergencies and storms, and providing other assistance as required.

The Transmission Contracts Analyst (or Senior) is also responsible for developing and managing a variety of transmission tariffs, contracts and agreements with Duke Energy transmission customers in accordance with company policies and procedures, applicable laws, and customer requirements. Key responsibilities include interfacing with transmission customers and transmission providers to develop, manage and ensure implementation of the terms and conditions of transmission tariffs, interconnection agreements, and generator interconnection agreements.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Coordinate the negotiation and execution of transmission service agreements and generator interconnection agreements. Communicate and coordinate with Corporate Accounting and Billing to ensure proper account setup and correct billing and payment posting in accordance with the requirements of the Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT).

- Develop a thorough understanding and in-depth knowledge of the Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) and the Federal regulations impacting the OATT.

- Monitor and maintain transmission customer accounts including regular contact and communications to answer questions and contribute to a positive working relationship with the transmission customers. Provide responses to the customers in a professional and timely manner.

- Determine credit worthiness of prospective customer and secure appropriate instrument to protect Duke Energy from undue credit risks. Possess a thorough understanding of various customers' Letters of Guaranty and various banks' forms of letters of Credit and effectively negotiate acceptance of these instruments with prospective customers, as appropriate. Provide updates to the approved customer lists and FERC Electronic Quarterly Report (EQR) based on credit related changes.

- Implement process measures for the Transmission Service Agreements process and participate in the development of transmission provider process measures.

Required/Basic Qualifications for Analyst

- Bachelor’s degree in Business or Other Related Degree

- In addition to required degree, five (5) or more years related work experience

Preferred Qualifications

- Bachelors degree in Electrical or Other Technical Degree

- NERC Certified Operator

Additional Preferred Qualifications

- Developing effective verbal and written communication skills in interfacing with internal and external customers

- Some prior utility industry experience (Generation, Transmission, Distribution)

- Possesses knowledge of Duke Energy transmission system and operating procedures, Duke Energy generation assets and operating procedures, FERC, NERC, NAESB, SERC and RFC standards and practices, utility practices, procedures and requirements concerning transmission operations, and general knowledge of RTOs

location_raw: Mt Holly, NC; St. Petersburg, FL; Cincinnati, OH
description:
Important Application Submission Information
In order to ensure your application is successfully received before the job posting expires, please submit your application by 11:59 PM on Friday, October 2, 2026
More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

Job Summary
The work within the Emerging Technology Office (ETO) is a critical part of Duke Energy’s corporate strategy through the demonstration and deployment of emerging technologies such as long duration storage, transportation electrification, distributed intelligence, and other customer products and services. There is an increased focus on these initiatives by the company with more urgent needs for data and integration of emerging technologies into daily operations.

The Technology Development Manager position will work on complex problems in engineering and emerging technology areas, with the ability to work independently and across multiple technical disciplines. A successful candidate will lead and coordinate strategic initiatives and project activities for the ETO, supporting the development and execution of technology assessment, evaluation and demonstration projects.

This position will be responsible for monitoring technology trends, facilitating cross-functional collaboration, and coordination throughout the technology development lifecycle. The employee will help develop project plans, coordinate project milestones and deliverables, facilitate stakeholder engagement, monitor project performance, and support the development of project documentation and reports.

Responsibilities and duties:
Technology Evaluation & Demonstration

- Monitor emerging technology trends, market developments, and industry activity to identify opportunities and inform ETO strategy.

- Provide analytical leadership for technology assessment, evaluation, road mapping, and emerging technology valuations.

- Manage emerging technology focused venture capital and external innovation relationships.

- Conduct engineering, research, and related studies of emerging technologies with areas of expertise and apply technical knowledge to support technology development decisions.

- Key technology focus areas include but are not limited to generation, energy storage, transmission and distribution, transformers, energy efficiency and demand response, electric vehicles, robotics, and artificial intelligence.

- Facilitate the development and execution of pilot project plans, ensuring alignment among project objectives, technical scope, stakeholder expectations, resources, timelines, and deliverables.

- Develop test plans, analyze test data, and communicate test results to key stakeholders.

- Apply necessary project management and control policies and standards for emerging technology initiatives, including planning, scheduling, resource coordination, risk management, and performance monitoring.

- Lead the full project lifecycle from opportunity identification and assessment through development, demonstration, technology transfer, and closeout.

Strategic Partnerships, Industry Engagement & Communications

- Develop and implement partnership strategies that support Emerging Technology organizational objectives.

- Build and maintain effective working relationships with internal stakeholders, industry partners, startups, universities, venture capital firms, and other external organizations.

- Lead industry benchmarking efforts and integrate external insights and lessons learned into ETO strategy and innovation practices.

- Lead ETO support for regulatory filings and other external or internal communications requiring technology development information.

- Represent the company at customer forums, industry organizations, trade associations, and other external engagements while exemplifying what it means to be a Duke Energy employee

- Lead education sessions, including lunch and learns, seminars, and tours

- Demonstrate effective oral and written communication skills and maintain accurate project records, documentation, and files.

Innovation & Organizational Enablement

- Support the development and continuous improvement of innovation, project lifecycle, technology transfer, and portfolio management processes.

- Assess and prioritize R&D activities with other Lines of Business (LOB) and ensure they are aligned with their technology roadmaps and Duke Energy’s strategic objectives.

- Support required legislative and/or regulatory programs, documentation and filings to ensure successful implementation of pilots/programs (e.g. NC Non-DSM/EE Rapid Prototyping)

- Contribute technical and analytical expertise to the identification, analysis, and resolution of problems in areas of specialization.

Basic/Required Qualifications:

- Bachelor's Degree in Information Systems, Engineering, or Computer Science

- Minimum of 7 years of related work experience.

- In lieu of degree, a High School Diploma/GED and a minimum of 11 years of related work experience

Desired Qualifications:

- Understanding of fundamental engineering theories, principles, and practices, with the ability to interpret technical information and apply it to business and technology development decisions.

- Demonstrated experience conducting technology assessments, gathering and analyzing industry data, developing business cases, evaluation alternatives, and making data-driven recommendations.

- Strong understanding of technology trends and drivers shaping the future of the electric utility industry and their potential business, operational, and customer implications.

- Demonstrate ability to work independently and effectively manage project and initiatives with ambiguous or evolving objectives.

- Demonstrated ability to lead and facilitate cross-functional teams and collaborate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all organizational levels.

- Demonstrated project management and project controls experience, including planning, scheduling, budgeting, resource coordination, risk management, and performance monitoring.
